Read a couple pages, writing down keywords. Don't write sentences or whole ideas, just keywords. After you've read 2-3 pages go to your list of keywords and try to recall what you read. Repeat, but instead of going back three pages worth of keywords, go back to the beginning of your list. If you write down entire concepts when you go back to your notes you are just rereading. If you exercise your brain by making sense of your keywords you can create a sort of muscle memory for those words and ideas.

This technique got me through grad school with a 3.9. You only have to do this process a few times before it becomes natural and you do it automatically without thinking. But you have to train your brain first, so the process might seem a bit tedious the first few times. It works though!

  1. Estimate amount of reading, depth of reading, and time: Flip through the assigned section to determine how much actual reading there is To set a pace and expectation. If it's twenty pages for a history exam I might give myself two hours to learn the material well. If it's twenty pages from a topical class (like gender studies) I might only estimate 30 minutes (and then read it like I do a magazine article).

  2. Skim the material reading headlines and maybe the intro of each section (this should only take 3-5 minutes, and it's just so you understand where the reading is going to take you. Also if it's a textbook, look at the review questions at the end of the reading. Those are the ideas you will be learning about

  3. Grab four different color highlighters and start reading. Anytime the author poses a new idea, highlight it one color. What is the authors thesis? Highlight it another color and any supporting statements throughout the text that same color. Any keywords or terms highlight a third color. Fourth color, highlight any critism of the thesis.

  4. Review your highlights. Go back and quickly skim only the sections you highlighted as thesis and supporting thesis. Does the thesis make sense? Does it match the direction you expected the reading to go? Does it match with the review questions? If so, good your on the right track. Go back and skim each highlighted section according to its color. This should only take 3-5 minutes. By now you should be comprehending the main concept.

  5. Now write it down! That main concept you just wrapped your brain around. Without looking at the text, write it in your own words. Now double check to see if it matches the reading. Take the time to also write down any thoughts you had, terms that are being defined, and questions you have.

  6. Take those notes to class and be a badass!
I like it. Doing #5 is absolutely crucial to having the ideas stored in memory such that they're integrated with other knowledge.

Iirrann soared high up in the skies, diving around and through the fluffy white clouds that floated lazily about. Behind him followed a true schryke beauty whose golden feathers were made to seem that much more golden by the illuminating rays of the sun, whose aerial grace was left unmatched. “I do not believe I could be any happier than I am in this moment” he said aloud as he turned toward the golden schryke. “Being with you, Kiriia, could not be more wonderful. I had only thought this moment could be possible in my dreams.” As soon as the final syllable departed from his beak, the bright skies around Iirrann turned dark and the whole world started to shudder. Only a few moments had passed before the shuddering stopped and Iirrann glanced around worriedly. “What was that?” he asked, turning to look quizzically at Kiriia only to discover her disappearance. The world began to shudder once again and soon Iirrann felt a sharp pain jolt up from the back of his skull.

Iirrann opened his eyes and stared at the ceiling of his tattered tent. “Damn” he whistled to himself. “I knew it was too good to be true.” The floor beneath him shuddered and caused him to jump to his feet. He sighed and rubbed his aching head. “These tremors are probably why I fell from my perch.” he thought to himself. “I should probably ask around and figure out what’s causing these.” He grabbed a few of his things that were lying around his tent and brushed open the flap covering the entrance to his tent. Outside there was a huge commotion. All sorts of people were running around screaming and battles between strange monsters and warriors of the schryke took place all across the marketplace. Only a few meters away stood Kiriia who was barely holding her own against one of the imposing creatures.

“Well, that can’t be right” Iirrann thunk. He stood up, stretched, yawned, and rubbed his eyes. “Ah, that’s better” he mumbled as he opened his eyes. All he could see was something dark and wet as his eyes began to focus. Something had surrounded him as he felt sharp and piercing pain along his neck, a sharp and piercing pain that would be the last sensation he would ever feel.
